sessions.title: Introductions and Basic Personal Information Practice
sessions.focus: Practice introductions, names, where you are from, and one or two easy follow-up questions.
sessions.summary: In this session, Wayne practiced introducing himself in Italian, stating his name and origin, and forming simple follow-up questions. The tutor maintained a gentle pace and encouraged Wayne to speak in Italian with minimal English support. Repetition of core phrases was used to build confidence, and attempts were rewarded to promote positive learning experiences.
strengths: Wayne can say 'Mi chiamo Wayne' with growing confidence.
He responds well to simple, familiar questions about identity and origin.
Shows good effort and maintains engagement despite beginner-level challenges.
needsWork: Pronunciation needs gentle correction to improve clarity, especially for phrases like 'Mi chiamo'.
Needs more fluidity moving from prepared phrases to natural follow-up questions.
Vocabulary remains limited to very basic introductions; more varied questions should be practiced.
nextDrills: Say aloud and repeat three times: 'Mi chiamo [your name]. E tu, come ti chiami?'.
Practice responding to 'Di dove sei?' with 'Sono di [your city]. E tu?'.
Ask and answer: 'Come stai?' with short replies like 'Bene, grazie.' or 'Così così.'.
Form three easy follow-up questions about origin and name to ask a partner: 'Come ti chiami?', 'Di dove sei?', 'Hai fratelli?'.
Listen and repeat a short dialogue introducing oneself and asking a simple question about origin.
cultureMoments: Discuss the importance of names and greetings in Italian culture, often accompanied by a handshake or kiss on the cheek.
Briefly introduce common Italian regions known for unique dialects in greetings, enhancing cultural awareness.
